chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a dog drinking from a vessel. He said, "Wash the vessel." And about the cat, he said, "There is no harm in performing wudu (ablution) from what remains of it; it is only one of the beasts."

key_terms.اغْسِلِ: wash; an imperative command indicating the legal ruling
key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: the vessel or container from which drinking occurred
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog, mentioned here regarding the ruling of impurity affecting a vessel
key_terms.فَضْلِهَا: what remains of its water after drinking
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicates permissibility

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dog or a cat drinks from a vessel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the purity laws related to water and vessels after animals drink from them. It distinguishes between the dog, whose vessel must be washed, and the cat, whose leftover water may still be used for wudu (ablution).
